en.title: Grace Greater than Our Sin
en.author: Julia H. Johnston
stanzas:
[G]Marvelous grace of our [C]loving [G]Lord,
[D7]Grace that exceeds our sin and our [G]guilt!
[G]Yonder on Calvary's [C]mount out[G]poured,
[D7]There where the blood of the Lamb was [G]spilled.

Sin and despair, like the sea waves cold,
Threaten the soul with infinite loss;
Grace that is greater, yes, grace untold,
Points to the refuge, the mighty cross.

Dark is the stain that we cannot hide.
What can avail to wash it away?
Look! There is flowing a crimson tide,
Brighter than snow you may be today.

Marvelous, infinite, matchless grace,
Freely bestowed on all who believe!
You that are longing to see His face,
Will you this moment His grace receive?
en.chorus:
[G]Grace, grace, [C]God's [G]grace,
[A7]Grace that will pardon and cleanse with[D7]in;
[G]Grace, grace, [C]God's [G]grace,
[C]Grace that is [G]greater than [D7]all our [G]sin.

notes: Text is the Cyber Hymnal (hymnary.org/hymn/CYBER/2013). Hymnary's representative text (Our Great Redeemer's Praise) differs in a few words: 'out-poured' and 'spilt' in st. 1, 'whiter than snow' for 'Brighter than snow' in st. 3, and 'all who are longing' for 'You that are longing' in st. 4 — 'whiter than snow' is the commoner printing and may be preferred. Date: hymnary says 1910, the Cyber Hymnal 1911 (Hymns Tried and True); the worklist's 1910 is kept. Meter is the text page's 9.9.9.9 with refrain; the tune page spells the same tune 9.9.9.9.4.9.4.9. Chords: MOODY's key is G Major already; the refrain's A7 is the secondary dominant this hymn is known for. Independently checked against Timeless Truths and HymnSite's UMH 365 (URLs appended; MOODY in G confirmed): UMH confirms 'What can avail' and 'Brighter than snow'; Timeless Truths prints 'What can we do to wash it away?' in st. 3 — a variant, not followed.
